The iconic San Siro played host to a captivating Serie A encounter as two heavyweights looked to assert their dominance in the league standings. With a packed crowd of over 73,000 spectators, the tension was palpable from the opening whistle as both sides prepared for a tactical battle. Atalanta's Clinical Opening On this May 2, 2026 , Atalanta started the match with incredible intensity, silencing the home crowd after just 7 minutes. Éderson was the quickest to react to a loose ball in the box, firing home with his right foot to give the visitors an early lead. AC Milan struggled to find their rhythm, and their frustrations grew when Davide Zappacosta doubled the lead in the 29th minute. After a brief VAR review to confirm the validity of the strike, the goal was given, highlighting a first half where the visitors were far more efficient in the final third. Raspadori Extends the Lead The second half began with more of the same as Atalanta continued to exploit gaps in the AC Milan defense. In the 51st minute, Marten de Roon and Éderson combined beautifully to set up Giacomo Raspadori , who clinically finished with his left foot to make it 3-0. The match seemed well beyond reach for the Rossoneri, who made several tactical substitutions, bringing on the likes of Pervis Estupiñán and Niclas Füllkrug to spark some life into their attacking play while the visitors focused on maintaining their structure. Late Drama and Milanese Resurgence Just as the game appeared to be heading for a comfortable away win, AC Milan mounted a furious late comeback. In the 88th minute, Strahinja Pavlović rose highest to head home a cross from Samuele Ricci , breathing life back into the stadium. Momentum shifted drastically, and in stoppage time, Marten de Roon conceded a penalty for a trip on Christopher Nkunku . After a VAR confirmation, Nkunku stepped up in the 94th minute to convert from the spot, making it 2-3. Despite the frantic closing stages, which saw yellow cards for Raoul Bellanova and Nikola Krstović amidst rising tempers, Atalanta held on to secure a narrow victory.

The Stadio Luigi Ferraris set the stage for a compelling Serie A encounter between Genoa and AC Milan on May 17, 2026. Both sides entered the pitch knowing that tactical discipline and clinical finishing would be the deciding factors in a match of high stakes. Tactical Stalemate in the Opening Period The first half was characterized by a cagey tactical battle where clear-cut opportunities were hard to come by. Santiago Gimenez provided a rare moment of individual flair in the 30th minute with an audacious bicycle kick that drifted wide of the target. As the halftime whistle approached, AC Milan ramped up the pressure, and Youssouf Fofana saw his goalbound header comfortably gathered by Justin Bijlow . Despite the territorial battle, both teams headed into the tunnels with the scoreline still level. Second-Half Breakthrough The game exploded into life shortly after the restart. In the 48th minute, a lapse in judgment from Genoa goalkeeper Justin Bijlow resulted in a penalty after he tripped Christopher Nkunku . The French forward stepped up to the spot and calmly converted with his right foot in the 50th minute, sending the keeper the wrong way. The opening goal sparked a more aggressive approach from both sides, leading to a flurry of yellow cards, including one for Vitinha for dissent as the intensity of the match heightened. Late Drama and Nerve-Wracking Finish As the match entered its final phase, AC Milan seemed to have secured the points in the 81st minute. Christian Pulisic turned provider, setting up Zachary Athekame , who unleashed a powerful strike from outside the box to make it 2-0. However, Genoa found a lifeline in the 87th minute when Johan Vasquez pounced on a defensive blunder by Koni De Winter to pull one back. The closing minutes were frantic; Niclas Fuellkrug missed a golden opportunity to restore the two-goal lead, and Bijlow made a stunning save to deny Pulisic in stoppage time. Ultimately, despite Genoa controlling 62% of the possession, AC Milan held firm to clinch a hard-fought victory.

On May 24, 2026 , the Serie A schedule brought together Lecce and Genoa for a clash that promised tactical intrigue and high intensity. Both teams looked to establish dominance early in a match where every small detail would carry significant weight for their league standings. Banda Strikes Early The contest ignited almost immediately as Lecce took a lightning-fast lead in the 6th minute. Santiago Pierotti turned provider, delivering a clinical ball to Lameck Banda , who made no mistake with a right-footed finish to put the home side ahead. The early breakthrough set the tone for a resilient defensive display, as Lecce absorbed the initial shock from Genoa while looking to exploit gaps on the break. Walid Cheddira had already threatened the visitors’ backline in the opening moments, though his efforts were frequently curtailed by the assistant referee’s flag for offside. Genoa Dominate Possession Despite falling behind, Genoa responded by seizing control of the ball, eventually commanding a staggering 68% of possession throughout the match. They pressed forward relentlessly, with Aaron Martin Caricol and later Jacopo Grossi swinging in numerous corners to test the home defense. However, clear-cut chances remained elusive. Lorenzo Colombo found himself isolated at times and was ruled offside twice during the first half, highlighting the disciplined defensive line maintained by the hosts. As the first half drew to a close, Ylber Ramadani received a yellow card, a sign of the increasing physical battle in the heart of the midfield. Resilient Defense Secures the Points The second half saw a series of tactical substitutions as Genoa desperately searched for an equalizer. The introduction of Brooke Norton-Cuffy and Latif Ouedraogo provided fresh energy on the flanks, but the Lecce defense remained resolute. Jamil Siebert and Tiago Gabriel were instrumental in the closing stages, making several vital interceptions to deny dangerous crosses aimed into the box. Even as the fourth official signaled three minutes of added time and the pressure reached its peak, Lecce stood firm. The final whistle confirmed a gritty performance from the hosts, who prioritized defensive organization to protect their narrow lead until the very end.
